# Awtarchy v4.0.0 Foot & Yazi Overhaul

Awtarchy v4.0.0 moves the managed Arch desktop to Foot as its primary terminal and delivers the latest Yazi file-management and text-input improvements. It also updates the integrated Quickshell, Hyprland, theme, and terminal-launching paths for the new terminal without removing existing Alacritty installations.

## Install and update

- New installations: [INSTALL.md](https://github.com/dillacorn/awtarchy/blob/main/INSTALL.md).
- Existing installations: [UPDATING.md](https://github.com/dillacorn/awtarchy/blob/main/UPDATING.md), or run `awtarchy update`.
- Stable updates install Foot when required and apply the published managed configuration. Existing Alacritty Graphics packages and personal Alacritty configuration are preserved; they are no longer Awtarchy-managed defaults.

## Foot terminal migration

- Foot from the official Arch repository replaces Alacritty Graphics as Awtarchy's default terminal across desktop launchers, keyboard shortcuts, terminal tools, Yazi integrations, and the transient PolicyKit authentication terminal.
- Managed Foot profiles preserve the familiar padding, font, 0.85 background transparency, and Hyprland compositor blur behavior.
- All nine Awtarchy color themes include complete Foot palettes. Theme changes recolor eligible already-open Foot terminals without restarting their shells, and new windows use the updated configuration.
- Prior Alacritty installations and `~/.config/alacritty` customizations remain available for optional personal use. Nothing automatically uninstalls Alacritty.

## Yazi input and navigation

- Ctrl+A selects the entire input text in Yazi rename, create, and tab-name prompts. Backspace and Delete remove highlighted text correctly; Ctrl+Z restores unsubmitted input edits while the prompt remains open.
- Normal cursor movement cancels a previous text selection before navigating.
- Creating a new tab restores automatic folder-based tab names instead of inheriting another tab's manually assigned name.
- Existing Foot mouse selection, Wayland clipboard integration, and managed Yazi file actions remain intact.
- Known limitation: reversing Ctrl+Shift+Left/Right during word selection can include one adjacent character due to current Yazi input behavior.

## Quickshell and compatibility

- The NetworkManager startup-order workaround remains in place. Runtime checks with Arch Quickshell 0.3.2 confirmed that a shell started before NetworkManager did not recover network devices, although a shell started after NetworkManager did; see [issue #275](https://github.com/dillacorn/awtarchy/issues/275).
- Suspend, monitor, and Bluetooth recovery helpers remain unchanged by that investigation. The separate legacy NVIDIA suspend investigation [#229](https://github.com/dillacorn/awtarchy/issues/229) remains open.

## Validation

- All 12 GitHub Actions workflow runs passed on the release target, `9ea76df9d2d9cdde6ab705d98c37f2a4785d61f5`.
- Foot migration PR [#276](https://github.com/dillacorn/awtarchy/pull/276) passed 30/30 GitHub checks. Foot 1.28 was additionally tested on an Arch/Hyprland machine: terminal configuration, theme palettes and live recoloring, transparency/blur, primary terminal, and PolicyKit integration.
- Yazi PR [#277](https://github.com/dillacorn/awtarchy/pull/277) passed 13/13 GitHub checks. The updated input and tab behavior was manually tested on the maintainer's Arch laptop.
- NetworkManager startup recovery and its working-startup control were tested locally on Quickshell 0.3.2; the required Awtarchy startup workaround was retained.
